name: hud
title: Hud
description: Everything true about the game right now, as one object: score, timer, lives, streak, and any other number as a stat. It is the library's first component made of components and it is deliberately thin, rendering no number, no glyph and no accessible-name vocabulary of its own. It carries no `data-gs-value`, because a HUD has no number and a container repeating one of the numbers inside it would give a test two elements answering for the same fact; `[data-gs-component="hud"] [data-gs-stat="score"]` finds the score. Parts it is not given are absent rather than zero, so a game with no lives system shows no hearts. Performs nothing itself, with the one exception it does not own: passing a timer starts a clock, exactly as rendering a timer would.
docs: Pass `score`, `timer`, `lives`, `streak` as the props each of those components takes, and the HUD renders the ones you passed, in that order. Pass `stats` for anything the four do not cover: a round, a rank, a multiplier, an XP total, each of them a `stat` so it gets the same typeface, the same tabular numerals and the same announcement rather than a second way of writing a number. Pass `placement` for where the group sits in whatever contains it; `left` and `right` render as a column. Read a number through the component that owns it, `[data-gs-component="score"] [data-gs-value]`, never through the first `[data-gs-value]` on the page: a HUD is four numbers and an unscoped selector now has four answers. Every rule in `hud.css` is scoped through `.gs-hud`, and that is a requirement rather than a style preference: a bare `.gs-stat` rule here would tie with the one in `stat.css` and a tie is decided by whichever stylesheet the bundler put last.
